accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding recent changes in the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets is correct?
o: The Greenland ice sheet alone has lost mass since 1993, while Antarctica has remained stable.
Significant ice-sheet mass loss has been observed only in the Arctic region.
Both ice sheets have been gaining mass continuously since 2000.
Both the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets have experienced significant mass loss for about two decades.
accepted.x: The Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets have both been losing significant mass for approximately two decades.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise global observation rather than accepting a reversed trend.
accepted.sec: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the State of the Global Climate 2025 report:
1. Oceans have absorbed more than 90% of the excess heat.
2. About 90% of the ocean surface experienced marine heatwaves in 2025.
3. The report recorded nine consecutive years of ocean heat records.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: oceans hold over 90% of excess heat, 2025 saw marine heatwaves over about 90% of the ocean surface, and ocean heat records continued for nine straight years.
accepted.tq: Use the coded combination to verify each numerical statement independently.
accepted.sec: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

accepted.s: According to the WMO State of the Global Climate 2025 findings, the approximate rise in global sea level since 1993 is
accepted.x: Global sea level has risen by approximately 11 cm since 1993.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely spaced numerical alternatives before selecting the reported value.
accepted.sec: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched with the WMO State of the Global Climate 2025 report?
o: Arctic sea ice—near record high; Antarctic sea ice—highest on record
Arctic sea ice—near record low; Antarctic sea ice—third lowest
Arctic sea ice—third lowest; Antarctic sea ice—near record high
Both Arctic and Antarctic sea ice—record high
accepted.x: The Arctic sea ice was near a record low, while Antarctic sea ice was at its third-lowest level.
accepted.tq: Compare the two regions carefully; the trap reverses their reported conditions.
accepted.sec: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

accepted.s: The glacier loss reported in the State of the Global Climate 2025 findings threatens water security for approximately
accepted.x: Glacier loss threatens water supplies for approximately 2 billion people.
accepted.tq: Recognise the scale of the impact from the numerical alternatives.
accepted.sec: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

accepted.s: In India during 2025, extreme weather events reportedly caused which of the following impacts?
o: 4,419 deaths and damage to 1.74 million hectares of crops
2,419 deaths and damage to 7.4 million hectares of crops
17,400 deaths and damage to 4.419 million hectares of crops
4,419 deaths and damage to 17.4 million hectares of crops
accepted.x: India recorded 4,419 deaths from extreme weather and crop damage covering 17.4 million hectares in 2025.
accepted.tq: Check both figures together; the distractors alter either the unit or the magnitude.
accepted.sec: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

accepted.s: The Antarctic sea-ice collapse since 2015 has been associated with which of the following processes?
o: Greenhouse gases and the ozone hole strengthened westerlies, lifting warm Circumpolar Deep Water.
The ozone hole reduced westerlies and prevented warm deep water from rising.
Declining greenhouse gases weakened westerlies and cooled Circumpolar Deep Water.
Increased snowfall alone caused the collapse of Antarctic sea ice.
accepted.x: Greenhouse gases and the ozone hole strengthened westerly winds, which lifted warm Circumpolar Deep Water and contributed to Antarctic sea-ice collapse.
accepted.tq: Trace the cause-and-effect chain instead of choosing a single-factor explanation.
accepted.sec: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Quelccaya—largest tropical ice cap, retreating about 200 feet per year
Okjokull—largest tropical ice cap of Peru
accepted.x: Quelccaya in Peru is the largest tropical ice cap and is retreating at approximately 200 feet per year.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure location-feature pair and reject the swapped glacier identities.
accepted.sec: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

accepted.s: Which glacier was declared the first 'dead glacier' in 2019?
accepted.x: Okjokull in Iceland was declared the first dead glacier in 2019.
accepted.tq: Directly distinguish the named glacier from other well-known ice bodies.
accepted.sec: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

accepted.s: The approximate annual thinning rate of the Greenland ice sheet mentioned in recent observations is
accepted.x: The Greenland ice sheet has been reported to be thinning by approximately 1 metre per year.
accepted.tq: Use the scale of the reported annual change to eliminate smaller and exaggerated values.
accepted.sec: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding warm-water coral reefs:
1. The 1.2°C threshold for large-scale reef collapse has already been crossed.
2. Recovery from mass coral bleaching generally takes more than 15 years.
3. Coral reefs are identified as among the most fragile climate tipping elements.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 1.2°C threshold has been crossed, recovery may take over 15 years, and warm-water coral reefs are considered highly fragile.
accepted.tq: Treat each statement as a separate threshold, recovery-time and classification claim.
accepted.sec: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

accepted.s: Climate change is reported to lengthen the duration of a day by approximately
accepted.x: Climate change is lengthening the day by approximately 1.33 milliseconds per century.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the decimal value and the time unit in a small scientific measurement.
accepted.sec: Observed global impacts - temperature, ice loss, dead glaciers, sea-level rise, extremes, coral bleaching

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Report)
a. State of the Global Climate
b. Global Annual to Decadal Climate Update 2026–2035
c. Greenhouse Gas Bulletin

accepted.s: The 2026 edition of the WMO's State of the Global Climate report characterised climate indicators as
accepted.x: The 2026 edition described the indicators as 'flashing red' and highlighted accelerating change.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact headline phrase rather than a general description of climate change.
accepted.sec: Global climate reports in news - WMO, IMD, Copernicus

accepted.s: According to the Global Annual to Decadal Climate Update 2026–2035, the projected warming for 2026–2030 is approximately
accepted.x: The update projects warming in the range of approximately 1.3–1.9°C for 2026–2030.
accepted.tq: Match the forecast range precisely; the distractors shift the lower or upper boundary.
accepted.sec: Global climate reports in news - WMO, IMD, Copernicus

accepted.s: Which of the following projections is associated with the Global Annual to Decadal Climate Update 2026–2035?
o: There is a 91% chance that at least one year will exceed 1.5°C, and 2027 may set a record.
There is a 50% chance that no year will exceed 1°C, and 2026 will set a record low.
There is a 91% chance that the entire decade will remain below 1.5°C.
There is a 19% chance that all years will remain below 1.5°C, and 2027 will be the coolest year.
accepted.x: The report gives a 91% chance of at least one year exceeding 1.5°C and indicates that 2027 may set a record; El Niño is expected late in 2026.
accepted.tq: Read the probability and projected year together; extreme reversal is the main distractor.
accepted.sec: Global climate reports in news - WMO, IMD, Copernicus

accepted.s: The WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin reported atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration of approximately what value for 2024?
accepted.x: The reported carbon dioxide concentration for 2024 was approximately 423.9 ppm.
accepted.tq: Check the leading digit and decimal value in the concentration figure.
accepted.sec: Global climate reports in news - WMO, IMD, Copernicus

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Lancet Countdown 2025?
o: Heat-related deaths declined by 23% since the 1990s.
Heat deaths increased by 23% since the 1990s, and dengue transmission potential rose by 85% in India.
Dengue transmission potential declined by 85% in India.
The report dealt exclusively with ocean acidification and sea-level rise.
accepted.x: The Lancet Countdown 2025 reported a 23% rise in heat deaths since the 1990s and an 85% increase in dengue potential in India.
accepted.tq: Watch for reversed trends and retain both figures in the correct combination.
accepted.sec: Global climate reports in news - WMO, IMD, Copernicus

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the World Meteorological Organization is correct?
o: It is a financial institution established in 1950 with headquarters at London.
It is a UN specialised agency established in 1950 with headquarters at Geneva.
It is a UN environmental programme established in 1988 with headquarters at Bonn.
It is a scientific panel established in 2007 with headquarters at Paris.
accepted.x: WMO has been a UN specialised agency since 1950 and is headquartered in Geneva.
accepted.tq: Use the organisation–status–date–headquarters combination to reject swapped institutional identities.
accepted.sec: Global climate reports in news - WMO, IMD, Copernicus

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC):
1. It was established in 1988 by WMO and UNEP.
2. It assesses scientific literature but does not conduct original research of its own.
3. It received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2007.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The IPCC was set up in 1988 by WMO and UNEP, assesses existing scientific literature rather than conducting its own research, and shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize.
accepted.tq: Verify the institution's origin, function and award as separate statements.
accepted.sec: Global climate reports in news - WMO, IMD, Copernicus

accepted.s: The year 2019 was recorded by the India Meteorological Department as India's
accepted.x: The IMD recorded 2019 as the seventh warmest year in India since 1901.
accepted.tq: Retain the ordinal ranking and its reference period together.
accepted.sec: Global climate reports in news - WMO, IMD, Copernicus

accepted.s: A climate tipping point is best described as a threshold at which
o: global temperatures immediately return to pre-industrial levels
only short-term weather changes occur without wider consequences
climate variations become completely predictable and reversible
small changes can trigger large, self-perpetuating and potentially irreversible shifts
accepted.x: A tipping point is a threshold beyond which small changes may produce large, self-perpetuating and irreversible shifts in a non-linear system.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition to distinguish a non-linear threshold from ordinary climate variability.
accepted.sec: Climate tipping points - meaning, elements, most fragile ecosystems

accepted.s: According to the Scientific Advisory Board brief, parts of the Amazon may change into savanna beyond approximately
accepted.x: Beyond approximately 2°C of warming, parts of the Amazon may shift from rainforest to savanna and turn from a carbon store into a carbon source.
accepted.tq: Match the threshold with the associated ecosystem transformation.
accepted.sec: Climate tipping points - meaning, elements, most fragile ecosystems

accepted.s: Which one of the following is identified as the most fragile climate tipping element among the listed ecosystems?
accepted.x: Warm-water coral reefs are identified as the most fragile tipping element, with their critical threshold already crossed.
accepted.tq: Select the specifically identified fragile ecosystem rather than a generally climate-sensitive biome.
accepted.sec: Climate tipping points - meaning, elements, most fragile ecosystems

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Amazon rainforest:
1. Approximately 17–18% of the Amazon has been lost.
2. The Amazon generates about 50% of its own rainfall.
3. Tree loss can disrupt the rainfall cycle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Loss of Amazonian trees can break the self-supporting rainfall cycle on which the forest depends.
accepted.tq: Combine percentage, ecological function and cause-effect statements without reversing the cycle.
accepted.sec: Climate tipping points - meaning, elements, most fragile ecosystems

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the other climate tipping elements listed by scientists?
accepted.x: Greenland and West Antarctic ice sheets, AMOC and permafrost are listed as climate tipping elements; Sahara Desert dunes are not included in that list.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the specific list rather than selecting a generally climate-related feature.
accepted.sec: Climate tipping points - meaning, elements, most fragile ecosystems

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between climate warming and species loss found in the Rutgers University study?
o: Land species are expected to disappear from habitats at twice the rate of ocean species.
Only freshwater species are affected by climate-related habitat loss.
Ocean and land species are expected to experience exactly equal habitat loss.
Ocean species may be wiped out from habitats at about twice the rate of land species.
accepted.x: The Rutgers study found that warming could eliminate about twice as many ocean species from their habitats as land species.
accepted.tq: Pay attention to the direction of the comparison; the principal trap reverses ocean and land.
accepted.sec: Biodiversity impacts - ocean vs land species loss, range shifts

accepted.s: The IPBES 2019 assessment reported approximately how many species globally, with up to how many threatened?
o: 80 million species, up to 10 million threatened
8 million species, up to 1 million threatened
accepted.x: IPBES estimated around 8 million species globally, of which up to 1 million may be threatened.
accepted.tq: Keep the total estimate and threatened subset in the correct order of magnitude.
accepted.sec: Biodiversity impacts - ocean vs land species loss, range shifts

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets correctly represents groups for which IPBES reported major proportions threatened?
o: 40% of amphibians, 33% of reef corals and over one-third of marine mammals
10% of amphibians, 20% of reef corals and one-third of marine mammals
40% of marine mammals, 33% of amphibians and one-half of reef corals
33% of amphibians, 40% of reef corals and one-tenth of marine mammals
accepted.x: The assessment reported that 40% of amphibians, 33% of reef corals and more than one-third of marine mammals were threatened.
accepted.tq: Match each percentage with its biological group; the distractors swap the figures.
accepted.sec: Biodiversity impacts - ocean vs land species loss, range shifts

accepted.s: The IPBES 2019 assessment was associated with which of the following descriptions?
o: It was conducted by UNEP in Nairobi without national participation.
It was conducted at Bonn by a body with 130 members, including India.
It was conducted by WMO in Geneva with 50 members.
It was conducted only by European countries and excluded India.
accepted.x: The IPBES 2019 assessment was associated with Bonn and involved 130 members, including India.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the assessment body, location and membership from nearby climate institutions.
accepted.sec: Biodiversity impacts - ocean vs land species loss, range shifts

accepted.s: As climate conditions become cooler toward higher latitudes and elevations, many species are expected to move
o: only toward the equator, irrespective of elevation
accepted.x: Species are shifting poleward and upslope as they track cooler climatic conditions.
accepted.tq: Apply the directional logic of following cooler conditions across latitude and elevation.
accepted.sec: Biodiversity impacts - ocean vs land species loss, range shifts

accepted.s: Which of the following ecological consequences has been associated with Antarctic sea-ice loss?
o: Disruption of krill and breeding failure among Emperor penguins
Increased krill abundance and improved Emperor penguin breeding
Recovery of coral reefs in Antarctic waters
Expansion of Antarctic sea ice and increased penguin breeding success
accepted.x: Antarctic sea-ice loss disrupts krill populations and contributes to Emperor penguin breeding failure.
accepted.tq: Link the physical change to its food-web and reproductive consequences.
accepted.sec: Biodiversity impacts - ocean vs land species loss, range shifts

accepted.s: The reported mass mortality of approximately 10 billion crabs occurred in the
accepted.x: Approximately 10 billion crabs were reported to have died in the Bering Sea.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive location–event association rather than a generic ocean option.
